title: The Teacher Who Carried a Spare Sari
subtitle: Savitribai Phule learned to read as a child bride. Then she taught the girls Pune didn't want taught.

inline.alt: Savitribai Phule's route: home, learns to read, trains, Bhide Wada, the walk, thrown out, school; then 1897, the last carry, the clinic
inline.caption: Her route: from learning to read, to the Bhide Wada school in 1848, to the plague clinic in 1897.

substack.email_subject: They threw dung at her on the way to school. She kept walking.
substack.note:
In 1848, men lined a teenage teacher's walk to school in Pune and threw dung, mud and stones at her. Eight years earlier, she couldn't read at all.

She never won the argument about whether girls should learn to read. She made it irrelevant, by teaching them anyway.
